cmd_link_add_refused: Error of `atlas -- <command>` when the running atlas dev refused the new service and gave no reason.
cmd_link_adhoc_usage: Error of `atlas --` with no command, in the shape of clap's usage line.
cmd_link_app_link_removed: Warning of `atlas unlink` for the desktop app when it was only a link with nothing saved. {command} is `atlas desktop`, in bold.
cmd_link_app_missing: Error of `atlas link --desktop --no-build` when the debug app bundle does not exist. {path} is where it should be.
cmd_link_backed_up: Result line of `atlas link` and `atlas link --desktop`: the release copy that was set aside, after a green check. Aligned with cmd_link_linked.
cmd_link_backup_failed: Error of `atlas link` and `atlas link --desktop`: copying the installed release file or app aside failed.
cmd_link_build_failed: Error of `atlas link` when `cargo build -p atlas-cli` exits with a failure; cargo printed its own errors above.
cmd_link_copy_failed: Cause line of an `atlas unlink` error: turning the link into a copy of the dev build failed.
cmd_link_create_failed: Cause line of an `atlas link` error: creating a folder failed.
cmd_link_creating_worktree: Progress line of `atlas wt create`, printed to stderr before the desktop app finishes the worktree.
cmd_link_desktop_build_failed: Error of `atlas link --desktop` when `cargo tauri build` exits with a failure.

cmd_link_desktop_needs_macos.description: Error of `atlas link --desktop` on a system that is not macOS.

cmd_link_desktop_not_installed: Error of `atlas <path>` when the desktop app is not running and not installed.
cmd_link_dev_busy: Error of `atlas -- <command>` when the running atlas dev does not answer in time.
cmd_link_dev_in_terminal: Error of `atlas -- <command>` when atlas dev runs in a terminal and cannot take a new service live. {root} is the project folder.
cmd_link_kept_as_copy: Warning of `atlas unlink` when no backup exists. {path} is where the backup would be. cmd_link_kept_as_copy_next follows.
cmd_link_kept_as_copy_next: Second line after cmd_link_kept_as_copy. {command} is `atlas update`, in bold.
cmd_link_launching: Result of `atlas <path>` when the desktop app was not running and is being started.
cmd_link_linked: Result line of `atlas link` and `atlas link --desktop`, after a green check: {link} is the installed file or app, now a symlink to {target}. Aligned with cmd_link_backed_up.
cmd_link_no_cargo: Error of `atlas link` when the `cargo` program cannot be started.
cmd_link_no_cwd: Error of `atlas link` and `atlas desktop` (dev mode) when the current folder cannot be read.
cmd_link_no_debug_binary: Error of `atlas link --no-build` when the debug binary of the workspace does not exist. {path} is where it should be.
cmd_link_no_home: Error of `atlas link` and `atlas unlink` when the system has no home folder for this user. Names the variable that holds it: USERPROFILE on Windows, HOME elsewhere. Same sentence as cmd_install_no_home; fold the two when both areas are on main.
cmd_link_no_tauri: Error of `atlas link --desktop` when `cargo tauri` cannot be started.
cmd_link_no_workspace: Error of `atlas link` and `atlas desktop` (dev mode) when no folder above the current one has a Cargo.toml with [workspace].
cmd_link_not_linked: Warning of `atlas unlink` when the installed atlas is not a symlink.
cmd_link_open_missing: Error of `atlas <path>` when the path does not exist.
cmd_link_opened: Result of `atlas <path>` when the desktop app is running. {path} is the project folder, or the file when it opened as a loose file.
cmd_link_rebuild_anytime: Line after `atlas link`. {command} is `cargo build -p atlas-cli`, printed in bold.
cmd_link_rebuild_desktop: Dim line after `atlas link --desktop`. {link} is `atlas link --desktop` and {dev} is `atlas desktop --dev`, both in bold.
cmd_link_reinstall: Line after cmd_link_removed_dangling. {command} is the install script command (curl ... | sh), in bold.
cmd_link_remove_link_failed: Cause line of an `atlas unlink` error: deleting a dangling symlink failed.
cmd_link_removed_dangling: Warning of `atlas unlink` when the link was dangling and nothing could be restored. cmd_link_reinstall follows.
cmd_link_replace_failed: Cause line of an `atlas link` or `atlas unlink` error: swapping the new file in failed. {path} is the file or app being replaced.
cmd_link_resolve_failed: Cause line of an `atlas <path>` or `atlas -- <command>` error: turning a path into an absolute one failed.
cmd_link_restore_failed: Error of `atlas unlink`: copying the saved release file or app back failed. {path} is the backup.
cmd_link_restore_release: Line after `atlas link`. {command} is `atlas unlink`, printed in bold.
cmd_link_run_failed: Cause line of an `atlas link --desktop` error: starting the setup script failed. {path} is the script.
cmd_link_runner_started: Result of `atlas -- <command>` when it started the runner. Same sentence as cmd_misc_dev_runner_started (`atlas dev --detach`); fold the two when both areas are on main.
cmd_link_save_failed: Cause line of an `atlas link --desktop` error: moving the new app backup into place failed.
cmd_link_service_logs: Detail line of `atlas -- <command>`: the log file of the new service.
cmd_link_service_port: Detail line of `atlas -- <command>`: the port the service listens on.
cmd_link_service_started: Result of `atlas -- <command>`. {service} is the name atlas gave the service.
cmd_link_setup_failed: Error of `atlas link --desktop` when the setup script of the repo exits with a failure.
cmd_link_symlink_failed: Cause line of an `atlas link` error: creating the symlink failed. {path} is the installed file or app.

cmd_link_symlink_windows.description: Windows only: the system's error for creating a symlink, with why it may have failed. {reason} is the system's error text.

cmd_link_title: Heading of `atlas link`, after a blue diamond.
cmd_link_unlinked_app: Result line of `atlas unlink` for the desktop app, after a green check. {path} is the app.
cmd_link_unlinked_binary: Result line of `atlas unlink`, after a green check. {path} is the installed binary.
cmd_link_workspace: Detail line of `atlas link`: the Cargo workspace of the atlas repo it links from.
